title: Allocate Minimum Number of Pages
description:
You are given an integer array `pages` of `n` books, where `pages[i]` is the number of pages in the `i`-th book, and an integer `students` representing the number of students.

You must allocate all `n` books among the students such that:
1. Each student is allocated at least one book.
2. Each book is allocated to exactly one student.
3. Allocation is contiguous — each student receives a contiguous subarray of books.

Return the minimum possible value of the maximum number of pages allocated to any single student. If a valid allocation is impossible (i.e., `students > pages.length`), return `-1`.
hints: First check the impossibility condition: if students > pages.length, it is impossible to give every student at least one book, so return -1.
Any valid answer must be at least max(pages) and at most sum(pages). Given a page cap M, greedily assign contiguous books to the current student until adding the next book would exceed M.
Binary search M in [max(pages), sum(pages)] for the smallest cap that requires at most `students` students.

examples.explanation: Allocating [12, 34, 67] (113 pages) to student 1 and [90] (90 pages) to student 2 minimizes the maximum pages to 113.
There are 5 students but only 3 books, so it is impossible for each student to receive at least one book; return -1.
With only 1 student, that student must read all books: 22 + 23 + 67 = 112 pages.
